summary: The Delta to wye conversion calculator turns the rb, the rc and the R₂ into R₁ (Resulting resistance values). That makes it useful for a lab report, a problem set or a sanity check on a physical situation. Every field is labelled the way you would say it out loud, so you can usually fill the form from memory and only look up the numbers you genuinely do not know.

sections.title: How does the Delta to wye conversion calculator work?
sections.html:
The Delta to wye conversion calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports R₁ (Resulting resistance values) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the operation); then you type in the rb (Delta to wye conversion), the rc (Delta to wye conversion), the R₂ (Wye to delta conversion) and the R₃ (Wye to delta conversion).

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Delta to wye conversion calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

R₁=rb × rc ÷ (rₐ + rb + rc)
Rₐ=R₂ × (-rb − rc) ÷ (R₂ − rc)
Rₐ=R₃ × (-rb − rc) ÷ (R₃ − rb)
R₁=-R₂ × R₃ ÷ (R₂ + R₃ − rₐ)
Rb=R₁ + R₁ × R₃ ÷ R₂ + R₃
Rc=R₁ × R₂ ÷ R₃ + R₁ + R₂

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Suppose Operation set to Delta to wye, Rₐ = 10 Ω, Rb = 10 Ω and Rc = 10 Ω. Working through the relationship above gives R₁ = 3.3333 Ω, R₂ = 3.3333 Ω and R₃ = 3.3333 Ω.

Read it as a template. Every number above can be replaced with one of yours; only the relationship between them is fixed.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: R₁ = 3.3333 Ω, R₂ = 3.3333 Ω and R₃ = 3.3333 Ω should be roughly the size you expected from Operation set to Delta to wye and Rₐ = 10 Ω.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Delta to wye conversion calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Testing whether an answer is physically plausible before you trust it
  • Solving a problem set where the algebra is more interesting than the arithmetic
  • Writing up a lab result and needing a quick cross-check
  • Any time the same 3 figures keep coming back — the rb, the rc and the R₂ — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Delta to wye conversion calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns R₁ (Resulting resistance values), derived from the rb, the rc and the R₂. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Delta to wye conversion calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the rb, the rc and the R₂, which is 7 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter rₐ (Delta to wye conversion) in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Rₐ (Delta to wye conversion) opens in ohms and the chip beside it offers 5 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There is one choice to make (1 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports R₁ = 3.3333 Ω. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Delta to wye conversion calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
